evidence.text: woman
Phonosemantic compound. 女 represents the meaning and 未 represents the sound.
女弟也。从女未聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *mɯːds): semantic 女 (“female, woman”) + phonetic 未 (OC *mɯds).
Probably Sino-Tibetan. Proposed etymologies:
* STEDT relates it to Proto-Sino-Tibetan *mi (“girl; female; feminine suffix”), whence Apatani nyimii (“girl; woman; female”), Proto-Loloish *C-mi² (“woman”), Proto-Karen *hmɨᴮ (“female; woman”).
* Schuessler (2007) compares it to Burmese မ (ma., “sister”) (whence အစ်မ (acma., “elder sister”), ညီမ (nyima., “younger sister”)), Miju ku-mai- (“woman”), Tibetan བུད་མེད (bud med, “woman”), and also Mizo hmei (“concubine”) (> Mizo hmei-chhia (“woman; wife”)), which STEDT relates to Proto-Sino-Tibetan *s-maj (“widow, widower”) instead.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Lexical Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解／甲金文字形與用例
evidence.text: The database analyzes the Shang oracle-bone and bronze forms as 女 semantic + 未 phonetic. It reports oracle-bone 妹 commonly used with the reading and sense of 昧, “before daybreak/dawn twilight”; bronze inscriptions use it for “younger sister” and also as a loan for 昧. Its examples include the Song gong Luan gui inscription “作其妹…媵簠” for the kinship sense, and the Da Yu ding phrase “女妹辰” read as 昧爽, dawn. The database then cites Shuowen’s 女弟 and the Odes’ 東宮之妹; it also notes the Yi’s broader 少女, “young woman,” usage. These are source interpretations and cited examples, not a secure chronology of the spoken senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 妹

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants)
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen gloss 女弟也 and analysis 从女，未聲, with fanqie 莫佩切. Its modern Mandarin reading is mèi. It separately glosses a younger female sibling, a younger woman of the same generation, a modest first-person address for a woman, and a young woman, citing classical and later literary examples. This supports attested extensions but does not establish when one sense developed from another.
evidence.title: A00902 妹 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 《说文解字》 entry reproduction and commentary
evidence.text: The page reproduces “女弟也。从女未聲” and displays forms labeled oracle bone, Spring and Autumn bronze, Shuowen seal script, Western Han clerical script, and Eastern Han clerical script. Those labels document the page’s form sequence; they do not by themselves prove a smooth graphic lineage. Duan Yucai quotes the Odes gloss 女子後生曰妹 and notes competing old explanations: 釋名 associates 妹 with 昧, while 白虎通 explains it with 末. The source records historical wordplay/analysis, not conclusive derivation from either word.
evidence.title: 说文解字：妹 — shuowen5.com

evidence.text: This modern reference labels 女 the meaning component and 未 the sound component, and lists oracle script, Spring and Autumn bronze, Shuowen seal, and Eastern Han clerical forms. Its historical pronunciation table gives 妹 as Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *C.mˤə[t]-s and Middle Chinese mwojH. These component and chronology statements are corroborative summaries; the page supplies no independent discussion of how the cited readings were established.

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese section (reconstruction data attributed there to Baxter–Sagart 2014 and Zhengzhang 2003)
evidence.text: For 妹, the page gives Middle Chinese mwojH, Baxter–Sagart system 1.1 (2014) Old Chinese *C.mˤə[t]-s, and Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003) *mɯːds. It identifies 未 as the phonetic component and lists Zhengzhang-series readings 妹 *mɯːds and 未 *mɯds. The reconstruction systems differ and must not be merged. The local Baxter–Sagart TSV independently records 妹 as *C.mˤə[t]-s and 未 as *m[ə]t-s; the 妹 row’s -s and uncertain [t] are preserved. No externally inspected page in this research yielded the exact Baxter–Sagart 未 row, so the TSV cross-check is local metadata rather than a separately verified upstream citation.

evidence.text: Exact local Baxter–Sagart notation: 妹 mèi, Middle Chinese mwojH, Old Chinese *C.mˤə[t]-s; 未 wèi, Middle Chinese mj+jH, Old Chinese *m[ə]t-s (two gloss rows); 女 nǚ, Middle Chinese nrjoX, Old Chinese *nraʔ, and 女 nǜ, nrjoH, *nraʔ-s. editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The oracle-bone reading is unsettled: CUHK describes it as commonly meaning dawn twilight, while an Academia Sinica abstract records both place-name and 昧爽 interpretations. That abstract could not be opened, so the competing arguments and exact earliest contextual attestations remain unresolved.
No inscription image was visually inspected. CUHK cites named bronze vessels and gives inscription text, but this report relies on the lexicon’s transcription and interpretation.

The date of the Song gong Luan gui inscription was not independently verified from an excavated-object catalogue; Spring and Autumn bronze is the broad period label shown by Dong Chinese for a bronze form.

A chronological semantic path from dawn twilight to younger sister is not established. Bronze sources attest both uses, and later classical sources document kinship and broader young-woman senses, but no source here demonstrates the semantic transition.

The 《詩·衛風·碩人》 and 《易·歸妹》 examples are textually ancient, but this search did not verify their manuscript dates or establish that their preserved wording is the earliest attestation of the respective senses.

The claim that 未 and 妹 are phonologically related is supported by component analysis and reconstruction comparisons, but ancient readings are reconstructed rather than directly recorded; modern Mandarin is not independent proof of the ancient sound relation.
The local Baxter–Sagart rows were inspected and preserved exactly; the official external source page for the exact 未 row was not verified. The local file is not treated as an external source URL.
Unicode Unihan GetUnihanData pages for 妹, 未, and 女 could not be accessed; the current-reading cross-check with official records was therefore incomplete.

No reliable evidence was found to establish a graphic corruption from 未 to 末 in 妹. Duan Yucai notes an older 末-based explanation, while Shuowen and the inspected paleographic dictionary give 未 as the phonetic element; these positions should remain distinguished rather than treating corruption as demonstrated.
A recent paper reports traditional place-name versus dawn interpretations of oracle-bone 妹, but its page failed to open. Further source inspection is required before adjudicating the disagreement.
The Sino-Tibetan comparisons in the imported Wiktionary excerpt were not investigated in this bounded search; no external comparative etymology is asserted here.

The official Xiaoxuetang result did not load the requested 妹 query correctly; no record-specific glyph or rights notice could be verified there. Commons gives a Sinica record identifier for the oracle-form redraw, but this run did not independently inspect that exact record.
No physical oracle-bone or bronze inscription image was inspected. The selected Commons images are modern redrawings of script forms.
The bronze-file search result turned up a Commons page for 妹-bronze.svg, but opening it failed; its exact original image URL and licensing details were not verified, so it is omitted.

The Da Yu ding phrase 女妹辰 is interpreted differently: the inspected transcription normalizes it to 汝昧辰 and glosses it as the owner’s childhood, whereas the dossier’s CUHK reference reports a dawn-twilight reading. This run does not resolve the disagreement or establish a secure early dawn sense.

This response is limited to external evidence and candidate glyph sourcing. It does not independently revalidate the dossier’s component phonology or Unihan current-readings; official Unihan pages remained inaccessible.

No image selected: previously attempted oracle and seal images were reported as HTTP 404 and are excluded; the alternate Commons bronze redraw’s exact description page failed to open, leaving its direct URL and license unverified. CUHK’s linked oracle-form page also failed to load.

CUHK reads some oracle-bone 妹 forms as 昧 ‘before daybreak’ and the Da Yu ding bronze phrase 妹辰 as 昧爽, while the dossier records an alternative reading of that phrase as childhood. This pass did not resolve the inscription reading or establish a semantic chronology from dawn to younger sister.

The evidence reviewed supports the traditional 女 + 未 analysis and later senses, but this pass did not independently check the readings of both 未 and 妹 in the local Baxter–Sagart table or official Unihan records. Do not use current Mandarin pronunciation as proof of an ancient sound relationship.
No physical inscription image was inspected; the image candidate was described as a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

The 1995 Academia Sinica article’s abstract challenges the CUHK dawn interpretation and proposes a negative reading related to 蔑; the full article’s evidence was not inspected, so this disagreement remains unresolved.
CUHK cites the Song gong Luan gui for a bronze kinship use, but this pass did not independently inspect an artifact catalogue or verify the vessel’s date.
The sources attest kinship, young-woman, broader younger-relative, and modest self-reference senses, but do not demonstrate a chronological semantic path among them.

The proposed oracle-bone dawn use and the possible loan spelling of 昧 remain disputed. No independently established source-word pronunciation or semantic relationship between dawn-related uses and the kinship word was found.
Official Unicode Unihan pages for 妹, 未, and 女 all returned access errors. Provided local kMandarin rows are preserved as local metadata, not represented as externally verified Unicode records.

The Xiaoxuetang evolution page loaded as a query page but yielded no textually readable form sequence; the form labels and dates could not be confirmed from its extracted contents.
Commons verifies a public-domain modern redraw labeled Shuowen seal style; no physical inscription image was visually inspected, and no artifact provenance or dating can be assigned to the redraw.

No evidence establishes that the 未 element in 妹 developed through graphic corruption from 末. Duan Yucai’s reported 末-associated explanation in the dossier remains historical commentary rather than demonstrated graphic ancestry.

items.period: Shang dynasty; file labels it Shang oracle script, with source notation 拾11.11, 合21568.
items.tradition: Shang oracle-bone script; modern vector redraw linked to Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang form 43.ECF6.
items.caption: A Shang oracle-script form of 妹 has a compact, dense structure near the upper left, with tall strokes rising above it, a long stroke descending on the right, and a broad lower form extending to the left.
items.alt: Black oracle-script glyph on white: a dense upper-left cluster sits beneath tall strokes; a long right stroke descends nearly to the bottom, and the lower form spreads broadly left.
items.selection_reason: This identified oracle-script form adds an early graphic example. Its shape does not settle how the character was read in oracle-bone contexts.
items.rights: Public domain/CC0 1.0 as stated on the Commons description page; Sinica separately dedicates query-interface glyph images and glyph attributes under CC0 1.0.

limitations.text: Oracle-bone readings remain disputed, with dawn-related, place-name, and negative interpretations proposed. The form alone cannot resolve these readings or establish a path to the kinship sense “younger sister.”
